title: A Home for the Stray Cat
summary: A girl finds a stray cat near her building and, with her family's help, learns the responsibility of caring for an animal before they decide together to keep it.
poll: A family should only keep a stray animal if every family member agrees to help care for it.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
Layla sees a thin cat near her building. The cat is scared. It runs and hides. The cat has no home. It is a stray cat.

Layla tells her mom. Mom says a pet needs care. It needs food and water every day. It needs a safe place to sleep. A pet is a big job. We must be responsible.

Layla gets an old box. She puts a soft blanket in it. This is a shelter for the cat. She puts out food and water.

The cat is scared at first. Layla is gentle and quiet. She waits. Soon the cat comes close. It eats. It drinks. It looks at Layla.

Dad takes the cat to the vet. The vet checks the cat. She is young. She has no owner. She needs shots to stay healthy.

The family talks. Layla will feed the cat every day. Mom and Dad say yes. The cat can stay! Layla names her Noor.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
On her way home, Layla sees a thin, stray cat near her building. The cat looks hungry and scared. It quickly runs away. It hides behind a bush.

Layla hurries inside. She tells her mom about the cat. Mom says that having a pet takes a lot of care. A pet needs food every day. It needs clean water every day too. It also needs a safe place to sleep. Taking care of an animal is a big job, so we must be responsible.

Layla decides to help the cat anyway. She finds an old box. She lines it with a soft blanket to make a small shelter. Then she sets out a bowl of food and a bowl of water nearby.

At first, the cat keeps its distance. Layla stays gentle and patient. She waits quietly instead of chasing it. After a while, the cat comes closer. It eats the food and drinks the water.

The next morning, Dad drives the cat to the vet for a checkup. The vet says the cat is healthy and young. She has no collar and no owner. She will need a few shots to stay safe from sickness.

That evening, the family sits together and talks about the cat. Layla promises to feed her and clean her bowl every day. Mom and Dad agree that the cat can stay. Layla happily names her Noor.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
On her way home from school, Layla notices a thin, stray cat crouched near her apartment building. The frightened animal looks hungry. The moment Layla steps closer, it darts away to hide behind a prickly bush.

Layla hurries inside and tells her mother all about the cat. Mom explains that having a pet is a real responsibility, not just a fun idea. A pet needs food every single day. It needs clean water every day too. It also needs a safe, warm place to sleep at night. Taking care of an animal takes real effort and time.

Still, Layla decides she wants to help the stray cat. She finds an old cardboard box. She lines it with a soft blanket, making a small shelter where the cat can rest. Then she sets out a bowl of food and a bowl of fresh water nearby.

At first, the nervous cat keeps its distance. Layla stays gentle and patient. She sits quietly instead of rushing toward it. Little by little, the cat creeps closer. It eats the food and drinks the water, then looks up at Layla.

The next morning, Dad drives the cat to the vet for a checkup. The vet explains that the cat is a healthy young female. She has no collar and no owner. She will need a few shots soon to stay safe from common illness.

That evening, the family sits together and talks about what to do. Layla promises to feed the cat and clean her bowl every day. Mom and Dad finally agree the cat can stay. A happy Layla names her new cat Noor, which means light.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
Walking home from school one quiet afternoon, Layla notices a thin, stray cat crouched beside her apartment building, its fur matted and its ribs faintly visible beneath patchy gray fur. The wretched animal looks frightened and malnourished, and the instant Layla steps closer, instinct sends it darting away to hide behind a prickly bush at the edge of the garden.

Layla hurries inside and tells her mother all about the cat she had just encountered outside, her voice rushing with excitement at the unexpected discovery. Mom explains that having a pet constitutes a serious obligation, not simply a charming idea that sounds exciting for a day or two before the novelty fades into tiresome daily chores. A pet requires food and clean water every single day, along with a safe, warm place to sleep at night, and someone must remember these duties even on busy or exhausting days when it would be considerably easier to neglect them entirely.

Still, Layla decides she wants to help the stray cat rather than simply walking past it the way most passersby do without a second thought. She finds an old cardboard box and lines it with a soft blanket, creating a temporary shelter where the cat can rest safely outside until the family reaches a decision about her future. Then she carefully sets out a bowl of food and a bowl of fresh water nearby, hoping the cat's instinct for survival will eventually draw it closer.

At first, the reluctant cat maintains its distance, watching Layla from behind the bush with wide, cautious eyes that track her every movement with evident suspicion. Layla remains gentle and patient, sitting quietly on the ground instead of rushing toward the frightened animal and frightening it further away. Little by little, over several long minutes, the cat creeps closer, consumes the food, drinks the water, and finally looks straight up at Layla as if gradually shifting its perspective from fear toward tentative trust.

The following morning, Dad transports the cat to the veterinarian for a thorough examination. The vet, a considerate woman who handles the cat gently throughout the checkup, explains that she is a healthy young female with no collar and, as far as anyone can determine, no owner searching for her at all. She will require several vaccinations soon to protect her from common illnesses that stray cats often contract while surviving outdoors independently.

That evening, the whole family sits together around the table and seriously deliberates what they should decide about the cat's future. Layla promises to maintain a daily routine, feeding the cat and cleaning her bowl every single day without ever forgetting, even on busy school mornings when sleeping in would feel considerably more tempting. Mom and Dad finally agree that they can adopt the cat, recognizing that the companionship she offers is well worth the obligation it brings, and a delighted Layla names her new cat Noor, which means light, because the small stray had brought genuine brightness into their once-quiet home.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
Layla first notices the stray cat on an ordinary afternoon, crouched beside her apartment building with matted fur and ribs faintly visible beneath its patchy gray coat. The wretched animal, frightened and clearly malnourished, follows its instinct the moment she steps closer, darting away to hide behind a prickly bush at the edge of the garden rather than risk approaching a stranger.

Rushing inside, Layla breathlessly tells her mother about the unexpected discovery. Mom's response is measured rather than enthusiastic: having a pet constitutes a serious obligation, she explains, not merely a charming idea that feels exciting for a day or two before the novelty fades into tiresome daily chores demanding real consistency. Food and clean water are required every single day, along with a safe, warm place to sleep at night, and someone must remember these duties even on exhausting days when neglecting them would be far easier.

Undeterred, Layla resolves to help the cat rather than simply walking past it, as most passersby would without a second thought. She lines an old cardboard box with a soft blanket, fashioning a temporary shelter where the animal can rest safely while the family deliberates her future, then sets out food and water nearby, hoping instinct will eventually draw the hesitant creature closer.

The cat, reluctant and suspicious, maintains its distance at first, tracking Layla's every movement with wide, cautious eyes. Layla responds with deliberate patience, sitting quietly rather than rushing toward an already frightened animal. Gradually, over several long minutes, the cat creeps forward, eats, drinks, and finally meets Layla's gaze directly, as though its perspective were shifting incrementally from fear toward tentative trust.

The following morning brings a visit to the veterinarian, where a considerate professional examines the cat gently and confirms she is a healthy young female, collarless and, as far as anyone can determine, entirely without an owner. Several vaccinations will soon be necessary, protecting her from illnesses that stray cats commonly contract while surviving independently outdoors.

That evening, the family convenes around the table to seriously weigh the cat's future. Layla commits to a consistent routine, promising to feed the cat and clean her bowl daily without exception, even on mornings when sleeping in would prove far more tempting than responsibility allows. Her parents ultimately agree to adopt the cat, concluding that the companionship she offers more than justifies the obligation involved, and a delighted Layla names her Noor, meaning light, because the small stray had brought genuine brightness into their household.

versions.title: A Home for the Stray Cat
versions.text:
Layla first notices the stray cat on an unremarkable afternoon, crouched beside her apartment building, its matted fur and faintly visible ribs betraying weeks of hunger beneath a patchy gray coat. The wretched animal, visibly frightened and clearly malnourished, obeys instinct the instant she approaches, darting away to hide behind a prickly bush at the garden's edge rather than risk trusting an unfamiliar stranger.

Rushing inside, Layla breathlessly recounts the unexpected discovery to her mother, who responds with measured consideration rather than immediate enthusiasm. Having a pet constitutes a substantial, ongoing obligation, she explains, not merely a charming notion that feels exciting for a day or two before the novelty inevitably fades into tiresome daily chores demanding genuine, unwavering consistency. Food and clean water are required every single day, alongside a safe, warm place to sleep, and someone must remember these obligations even on exhausting days when neglecting them would prove considerably more convenient.

Undeterred, Layla resolves to assist the cat rather than simply walking past, as most indifferent passersby would without a second thought. She lines an old cardboard box with a soft blanket, fashioning a temporary shelter where the animal can rest safely while the family deliberates her uncertain future, then arranges food and water nearby, hoping instinct will eventually draw the hesitant, reluctant creature closer.

The cat, plainly reluctant and deeply suspicious, maintains its distance initially, tracking Layla's every movement with wide, cautious eyes that betray lingering distrust. Layla responds with deliberate, unhurried patience, sitting quietly rather than rushing toward an already frightened animal and compounding its distress unnecessarily. Gradually, over several protracted minutes, the cat creeps forward, eats, drinks, and finally meets Layla's gaze directly, as though its perspective were shifting incrementally from instinctive fear toward tentative, provisional trust.

The following morning brings a visit to the veterinarian, where a considerate professional examines the cat gently and confirms she is a healthy young female, collarless and, as far as anyone can determine, entirely without an owner. Several vaccinations will soon prove necessary, protecting her from illnesses that stray cats commonly contract while surviving independently outdoors, exposed continually to disease, hunger, and injury alike.

That evening, the family convenes around the table to seriously weigh the cat's uncertain future. Layla commits herself to a consistent, unwavering routine, promising to feed the cat and clean her bowl daily without exception, even on mornings when sleeping in would prove far more tempting than responsibility typically allows. Her parents ultimately agree to adopt the cat, concluding that the companionship she offers more than justifies the obligation it inevitably entails, and a delighted Layla names her Noor, meaning light, because the small, once-wretched stray had brought genuine brightness into their once-quiet household.

LOW.modelAnswer: I would want to help a stray animal like Layla did. In the story, Layla made a shelter with a box and a soft blanket so the cat had a safe place to rest. She also gave the cat food and water and was gentle so it would not be scared. I think helping an animal that has no home is a kind and responsible thing to do.

keyWords.definition: to take an animal, or sometimes a child, into your family to care for permanently
keyWords.example: Our neighbors decided to adopt a puppy from the animal shelter.

keyWords.definition: a set of things you do regularly, usually in the same order
keyWords.example: Brushing his teeth every morning is part of my brother's daily routine.

keyWords.definition: slow to act or decide because you feel unsure
keyWords.example: She was hesitant to raise her hand even though she knew the answer.

keyWords.definition: lasting for only a short time, not permanent
keyWords.example: The school set up a temporary classroom while the new building was finished.

keyWords.definition: careful not to upset or inconvenience other people or animals; thoughtful
keyWords.example: A considerate neighbor keeps the noise down late at night.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the central idea of the story?
options: Layla learns that running her own pet store downtown is easy.
Layla and her family learn to care for a stray cat and decide to adopt her.
Layla's family firmly decides a stray cat can never really be trusted.
The vet flatly refuses to help any cat that has no listed owner.
questions.why: The story follows the stray cat from being found, to being cared for and checked by a vet, to being adopted as the family learns about responsibility.

wrong.A: The story is not about owning a pet store.
wrong.C: The family ends up trusting and keeping the cat.
wrong.D: The vet helps the cat with a checkup and shots.

questions.stem: What does Mom explain to Layla before they decide to help the cat?
options: That the vet's office is too far away to visit today
That cats are not allowed to live in their apartment building
That having a pet takes real daily effort
That Layla should first try to find the cat's old owner
questions.why: Mom explains that a pet needs food, water, and a safe place every day, and that this takes real effort.

wrong.A: Distance to the vet is not mentioned.
wrong.B: The story does not say pets are banned in the building.
wrong.D: The vet later confirms the cat has no owner, but this is not what Mom explains.

questions.stem: What does Layla build for the cat, and why?
options: A tall fence, to keep the cat from running far away
A bed indoors, because the cat is allowed inside right away
A temporary shelter made from a box and blanket
A paper sign, to help the cat find its old owner again
questions.why: Layla lines an old box with a blanket to create a temporary shelter outside for the cat.

wrong.A: The story does not mention a fence.
wrong.B: The cat is not brought indoors right away.
wrong.D: There is no sign in the story.

questions.stem: Why does the cat slowly come closer instead of staying hidden?
options: It suddenly smells another cat somewhere nearby
A loud noise scares it out from behind the bush
The vet calls the cat over from far away
Layla's patience and gentle care slowly earn its trust
questions.why: Because Layla waits quietly and offers food and water, the hesitant cat gradually feels safe enough to approach.

wrong.A: No other cat is mentioned.
wrong.C: The vet is not present at this point in the story.

questions.stem: In the story, the word hesitant means —
options: feeling angry and ready to fight about it
feeling unsure and slow to act, full of doubt
feeling completely unafraid of anything at all
feeling excited and eager to act right away
questions.why: The hesitant cat keeps its distance and is slow to approach because it is unsure whether to trust Layla.

wrong.A: The cat is frightened, not angry.
wrong.C: The cat is clearly afraid, not unafraid.
wrong.D: The cat is the opposite of eager at first.

questions.stem: Why does the family decide to adopt the cat instead of just helping her once?
options: Because the cat already has a collar with their address on it
Because no animal shelters exist anywhere nearby at all
Because the vet strictly orders them to keep the cat
Because Layla promises daily care and the family agrees
questions.why: The family discusses the cat's future, and they decide to adopt her once Layla commits to feeding and caring for her every day.

wrong.A: The cat has no collar at all.
wrong.B: The story never discusses other shelters.
wrong.C: The vet only gives information; the family makes the decision.

questions.stem: How is the story organized?
options: It lists facts about different kinds of cats
It compares two different families who both find cats
It follows the story's events in order, from start to finish
It carefully explains exactly how vets are trained
questions.why: The story moves step by step through finding the cat, building a shelter, the vet visit, and the family's final decision.

wrong.A: This is a narrative, not a list of facts.
wrong.B: Only one family and one cat appear in the story.

questions.stem: What can you infer about why Layla is especially careful and considerate with the cat?
options: She wants to impress her parents more than help the cat
She understands the cat is frightened and needs patience
She is told by the vet exactly what to do, step by step
She has read every single book about cats ever written
questions.why: Layla's calm, patient actions show she understands the cat is scared and needs gentle care to build trust.

wrong.A: The story shows Layla's care is about the cat's wellbeing, not about impressing anyone.
wrong.C: The vet appears later, after Layla has already been caring for the cat.
wrong.D: The story never mentions Layla reading books about cats.

MID.prompt: Explain the steps Layla's family took to decide whether to keep the stray cat. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained the steps the family took in order.
I used at least two details from the story.
MID.modelAnswer: Layla's family took several steps before deciding to keep the stray cat. First, Layla made a temporary shelter from a box and blanket and gave the cat food and water. Then her dad took the cat to the vet, who checked that she was healthy and had no owner. Finally, the whole family talked together, and Layla promised to follow a daily routine of feeding and caring for the cat, which helped them decide to adopt her.

keyWords.definition: the comfort or friendship that comes from spending time with someone, including an animal
keyWords.example: After moving to a new city, he found companionship in his loyal old dog.

keyWords.definition: a duty or responsibility that someone feels they must fulfill
keyWords.example: Returning a borrowed book on time is a small but real obligation.

keyWords.definition: a particular way of thinking about or viewing a situation
keyWords.example: Traveling to a new country gave her a fresh perspective on her own home.

keyWords.definition: unwilling or hesitant to do something
keyWords.example: He was reluctant to try the spicy dish, but he tasted it anyway.

keyWords.definition: a natural tendency to behave in a certain way without being taught
keyWords.example: Birds build nests by instinct, without anyone teaching them how.

questions.stem: Which statement best captures the central idea of the story?
options: Owning a pet guarantees instant companionship with no effort required.
Veterinarians should decide which animals families are allowed to keep.
Caring responsibly for a frightened stray cat, step by step, leads a family to recognize that the obligation is worth taking on.
A stray animal's instincts can never be changed by human kindness.
questions.why: The narrative traces the family's gradual, deliberate process of caring for the cat, which ultimately persuades them that adopting her is worthwhile despite the obligation involved.

wrong.A: The story emphasizes that companionship requires real effort, not that it is instant.
wrong.B: The vet provides information but does not make the family's decision.
wrong.D: The cat's instinctive caution does shift as trust develops.

questions.stem: Why does the stray cat initially flee when Layla approaches?
options: It is following another cat that signaled danger
It has been trained to avoid children specifically
It is instinctively cautious of an unfamiliar person
It recognizes Layla as someone who has mistreated animals before
questions.why: As a frightened stray with no prior relationship to Layla, the cat's instinctive wariness of an unfamiliar human causes it to flee and hide.

wrong.A: No other cat appears in the story.
wrong.B: No training of this kind is mentioned.
wrong.D: Nothing suggests Layla has mistreated animals.

questions.stem: What does Mom's explanation reveal about her perspective on pet ownership?
options: She thinks only adults should be responsible for animals
She wants to avoid the cat entirely to prevent any obligation
She believes pets are more trouble than they are worth
She views it as a genuine, ongoing obligation rather than a passing novelty
questions.why: Mom stresses that a pet requires daily care and commitment, framing pet ownership as a serious, lasting obligation rather than a brief source of excitement.

wrong.A: She involves Layla directly in the responsibility rather than excluding her.
wrong.B: The family does not avoid the cat; they actively help her.
wrong.C: She does not say pets are not worth it; she ultimately agrees to adopt.

questions.stem: In the story, the word reluctant most nearly means —
options: completely fearless
unwilling or hesitant
deliberately aggressive
enthusiastic and eager
questions.why: The reluctant cat keeps its distance and is slow to trust, showing hesitation rather than eagerness, fearlessness, or aggression.

wrong.A: The cat is visibly afraid, not fearless.
wrong.C: Nothing suggests the cat behaves aggressively.
wrong.D: The cat's behavior is the opposite of eager at first.

questions.stem: Based on the story, what most likely allows the cat's perspective to shift from fear toward trust?
options: A sudden change in the weather
The vet's examination the following morning
The family's decision to adopt her
Layla's consistent gentleness combined with the patient offering of food and water over time
questions.why: The gradual shift happens before the vet visit or adoption decision, driven by Layla's repeated, patient, gentle approach that slowly earns the cat's trust.

wrong.A: Weather is not mentioned as a factor.
wrong.B: The vet visit occurs after the cat has already begun to trust Layla.
wrong.C: The adoption decision comes even later, after trust has developed.

questions.stem: Place these events in the order they happen in the story.
options: The vet confirms the cat has no owner; the family adopts her; Layla builds a shelter
The family adopts the cat; Layla builds a shelter; the vet examines her
Layla builds a temporary shelter; the vet confirms the cat has no owner; the family adopts her
The cat approaches Layla; the family adopts her; Layla builds a shelter
questions.why: Layla first builds the shelter and feeds the cat, then the vet examines her and confirms she has no owner, and only afterward does the family decide to adopt her.

wrong.A: The shelter is built before the vet visit, not after.
wrong.B: The adoption decision comes last, not first.
wrong.D: The shelter is built before the cat fully approaches, and adoption comes after the vet visit.

questions.stem: What can readers infer about why the family's discussion at the table matters to the story's meaning?
options: It shows that Mom and Dad always overrule Layla's wishes
It proves that the vet's opinion is irrelevant to the decision
It shows that the family regrets finding the cat at all
It shows that decisions about shared responsibility are best made together, with everyone's commitment considered
questions.why: The family discussion, including Layla's promise of a daily routine, suggests that taking on a shared obligation works best when every member agrees and commits to their part.

wrong.A: The parents ultimately agree with Layla rather than overruling her.
wrong.B: The vet's confirmation that the cat is healthy and ownerless informs the family's decision.
wrong.C: The ending shows satisfaction, not regret.

questions.stem: Why does the author include the detail that Noor's name means light?
options: To explain a scientific fact about cats' eyes
To suggest the cat glows in the dark
To describe the color of the cat's fur
To emphasize how the cat's presence brought warmth and joy into the family's life
questions.why: Naming the cat Noor, or light, symbolically reflects the positive change and companionship she brings to the household, reinforcing the story's theme.

wrong.A: The detail is about the cat's name, not eye science.
wrong.C: The cat's fur is described as gray, unrelated to the meaning of her name.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says a family should only keep a stray animal if every family member agrees to help care for it. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about obligation, trust, and companionship.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that a family should only keep a stray animal if everyone agrees to help care for it. In the story, Mom explains that a pet is a real obligation requiring daily food, water, and attention, not just a passing novelty, and the family only decides to adopt Noor after Layla specifically promises to maintain a daily routine of care. Someone might argue that a single caring person, like Layla, is enough to take on the responsibility alone. However, the story shows the whole family discussing the decision together at the table, which suggests that shared commitment makes the companionship and obligation easier to sustain over time.
